name: AMS-100
summary: AMS-100 is a high-acceptance space cosmic-ray and antimatter observatory concept for a proposed Sun–Earth L2 orbit. Its name must not be interpreted as an approved AMS-02 upgrade.
detection_principle: A high-acceptance superconducting magnetic spectrometer measures charge sign, rigidity and species of charged cosmic rays, combining deep calorimetry for antiparticles and gamma rays to test rare antimatter components related to dark matter.

results.summary: Key-component prototype-development performance has been published; no space dark-matter observations by AMS-100 yet.

science_scope: Searches cosmic gamma-ray, antiparticle or neutrino spectra, directions and fluxes for indirect signatures of dark-matter annihilation, decay or related new physics. Conventional astrophysical sources and propagation can produce similar signals, requiring background modeling; design sensitivity is not a measured limit or discovery.
